'''''Hymenocallis latifolia''''' ('''mangrove spider-lily''' or '''perfumed spider-lily''') is a bulb-forming perennial that grows on beaches, sand dunes, mangrove swamps and other wetlands along the coasts of [[Florida]], [[Mexico]], and the [[West Indies]] ([[Cuba]], [[Jamaica]], [[Puerto Rico]], [[Cayman Islands]], [[Bahamas]], etc.).<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/33505490#page/444/mode/1up Roemer, Max Joseph.,  Familiarum Naturalium Regni Vegetabilis Synopses Monographicae 4: 168. 1847.] in Latin</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/1200411 Tropicos, ''Hymenocallis latifolia'' (Mill.) M. Roem.]</ref><ref>[https://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=278840 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[https://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Hymenocallis%20latifolia.png Biota of North America Program 2013 county distribution map]</ref> It has showy white flowers and large green seeds up to 2.5 cm in diam. Common names include "mangrove spider-lily," "perfumed spider-lily," <ref>Flora of North America, v 26, p 292.</ref>
